records.title: A Case of Mixed Decompression Illness Manifestations in a Commercial DC-8 Cargo Jet Pilot
records.author: Stephen J. H. Veronneau; Andrew A. Pilmanis; Stanley R. Mohler
records.locator: FAA case, Sequence of Events, Medical Findings and Discussion
records.note: One clinically described pilot from a selected commercial cargo incident. The FAA medical authors describe mixed DCS and arterial gas embolism features. The NTSB investigation attributes incapacitation to decompression sickness. The clinical case is indexed once as mixed decompression illness. No inception cohort or independent exposure denominator is available. NTSB crew statements place radio nonresponse near FL290 while climbing. The FAA narrative places rapid incapacitation after about four minutes at FL330. These are different observations of impairment. First clinical symptom time and cabin pressure history are unknown.

records.title: Aviation Investigation Final Report, NYC94LA062
records.author: National Transportation Safety Board
records.locator: NTSB NYC94LA062 final report, pp. 1, 3, 5 and 6, Analysis and Factual Information
records.note: Same event as the FAA case. On March 15, 1994 the DC-8-61 diverted to Greater Cincinnati at Covington after the captain became incapacitated. The final report counts one serious crew injury. This is an investigator attribution, with the FAA clinical source retaining mixed DCI.
